argument.text: By H003 and H004, h y^0v=λv. For the h-identity, assume the induction hypothesis L1: hy^d v=(λ-2d)y^dv. Then hy^(d+1)v=(yh-2y)y^dv=(λ-2d-2)y^(d+1)v. Discharging L1 and using induction proves the h-identity for every d≥0. Also xyv=(yx+h)v=λv. For the x-identity, at an arbitrary d≥1 assume L2: xy^dv=d(λ-d+1)y^(d-1)v. The just proved h-identity gives xy^(d+1)v=(yx+h)y^dv=[d(λ-d+1)+λ-2d]y^dv=(d+1)(λ-d)y^dv. Discharging L2 and inducting from d=1 proves the x-identity. The d=0 x-value is xv=0. These are identities of complex vectors; no reduction of weights has occurred.

produces.statement: For every integer d≥0, hy^dv=(λ-2d)y^dv; xv=0, and for every d≥1, xy^dv=d(λ-d+1)y^(d-1)v.

argument.text: H001 implies n>0 and |I|=λ+1=n. Iterating F001 gives x^i y^iv=i!·λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v for i∈I. Every factor in this product is nonzero over C when i≥1, and the i=0 product is one; H004 therefore gives e_i≠0. Also he_i=(λ-2i)e_i by F001. The eigenvalues λ-2i are pairwise distinct over C. Assume L3: Σ_{i∈I}α_i e_i=0. For arbitrary j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id_V). All terms except the j-th vanish, leaving α_j·(∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k-j))e_j=0. Its vector and scalar product are nonzero (empty product one), so α_j=0. Discharge L3: every relation is trivial. There are n independent vectors and dim_C V=n by H002, hence they form a basis.

produces.statement: n>0, |I|=n, and (e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V with each e_i nonzero and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i.

argument.text: F001 at d=λ+1 gives h y^(λ+1)v=(-λ-2)y^(λ+1)v. Expanding this vector in the basis F002, the equation says that its coefficient at every e_i is killed by (λ-2i)-(-λ-2)=2(λ+1-i), nonzero over C for i∈I. Thus y^(λ+1)v=0; equivalently a nonzero vector of this eigenvalue would contradict the basis spectrum. Applying further powers of y gives y^dv=0 for all d>λ.

produces.statement: For all integers d>λ, y^dv=0.

argument.text: For i∈I the definitions and F001 give xe_0=0 and xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_(i-1) for i≥1. They also give ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0 by F003, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. Iterating these formulas r times and dividing by r! yields X_r e_i=[(λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!]e_(i-r)=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) for r≤i, and Y_r e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_(i+r)=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) for i+r≤λ. The products are empty when r=0. Otherwise the x-string reaches e_0 and is killed, or the y-string passes e_λ and is killed, so the remaining cases give zero. These coefficients are integers by the usual finite binomial formula. Together with F001–F003 this proves every clause of N001.

argument.text: By H001, 0∈I and n>0. Use the injection and identification in N002. For each i∈I, E_ii maps M_R onto J_i e_i: its image is contained there by coordinate projection, and it fixes every c e_i in that submodule. This image is finitely generated because the images of the n members of an R-basis of M_R generate it. Since e_i≠0 by N001, multiplication by e_i identifies J_i with J_i e_i, so J_i is finitely generated. If c∈J_j, then c e_j∈M_R and E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i∈M_R by N002; hence J_j⊆J_i. Reversing i,j proves equality, and each equals J_0=J. At least one coordinate image is nonzero, since otherwise M_R would be zero, contradicting that its complex span is the nonzero V with n>0. Thus the common J is nonzero.

argument.text: Each vector of M_R is the sum of its coordinate projections E_ii, so F001 places it in Σ_{i∈I}J e_i. Conversely each of these coordinate submodules is contained in M_R by definition. The sum is direct because (e_i) is a complex basis by N001: a relation Σc_i e_i=0 with c_i∈J⊆C forces every coefficient to vanish. Thus the coordinate-sum map J^I→M_R is an R-linear bijection, with inverse given by its coordinates. N001 supplies n>0 and the basis of V, and N002 supplies injectivity, rank n and complex spanning, giving all the other exported clauses.

hypothesis_checks: Q is a field and hence a semiring with the strong rank condition: injectivity carries a linearly independent family of s vectors into Q^t, forcing s≤t by finite-dimensional linear algebra.

argument.text: By N003, J⊆C is finitely generated and nonzero, and M_R is free of rank n with coordinate decomposition J^I. Define T=Q⊗_R J and θ(q⊗c)=qc. The fraction field of R is Q: integers lie in R and every rational is a quotient of two nonzero elements of R. To see the multiplication map is injective, write any finite tensor sum over a common nonzero denominator s∈R as (1/s)⊗c with c∈J. If θ sends it to zero then c/s=0 in C, so c=0, and the tensor is zero. This also gives the usual identification of this tensor product with the localization of J. A finite R-generating family of J yields a finite Q-spanning family of T by tensoring; consequently T is finite dimensional. This proves the localization injectivity used here without presuming that containment J⊆C implies rank one.

produces.statement: T=Q⊗_R J is a finite-dimensional Q-vector space, θ:T→C is injective with image equal to the Q-linear span of J.

argument.text: Set r=dim_Q T. Tensor the R-coordinate isomorphism in N003 with Q. The result is a Q-linear isomorphism Q⊗_R M_R≅T^I: tensor the coordinate maps in each direction, and identify Q⊗_R J^I with T^I by q⊗(c_i)_i↦(q⊗c_i)_i, whose inverse sums the tensors supported at one coordinate. Finite I makes these mutually inverse. An R-basis of M_R of n members, supplied by N003, extends to a Q-basis of Q⊗_R M_R; its coefficient maps extend and prove both spanning and independence. Its dimension is therefore n. Apply M001 to the finite product T^I over Q: F001 gives finite dimension, hence a finite basis and finite generation; Q has the strong rank condition by the usual finite independent-family bound. M001 gives dim_Q T^I=Σ_{i∈I}dim_Q T=nr, using |I|=n. Thus n=nr, so r=1 because n>0 by N003. By F001, θ identifies T with a one-dimensional rational subspace of C containing J. In particular, for any nonzero a∈J and any c∈J there is a unique q∈Q with c=qa.

produces.statement: dim_Q T=1 and θ(T) is the one-dimensional Q-linear span of J in C. For every nonzero a∈J and every c∈J there is a unique rational q with c=qa, and q≠0 when c≠0.

argument.text: Choose 0≠a∈J and a nonempty finite generating family g of nonzero elements of J using N003. By F002, write its members as g_j=q_j a with q_j∈Q×. For each such rational q_j, removing all powers of the prime p from its nonzero integer numerator and denominator gives q_j=p^{d_j}u_j, where d_j∈Z and both u_j and u_j^(-1) lie in R: neither the remaining numerator nor denominator is divisible by p. This is just finite factorization by repeated division of nonzero integers by p, and works for positive or negative exponents and signs. The resulting finite family of integer exponents is nonempty.

produces.statement: g is a nonempty finite R-generating family of J, g_j=q_j a with a≠0 and every q_j∈Q×. Each q_j has a p-order d_j∈Z with q_j=p^{d_j}u_j for a unit u_j∈R. The finite set of these p-orders is nonempty.

argument.text: Let d be the family of exponents from F003, let ν=min_j d_j, and define b=p^ν a. Since p is prime and a≠0, b≠0. For every generator q_j a, its ratio to b is p^{d_j-ν}u_j∈R because d_j≥ν. Thus J⊆Rb. For an index attaining the minimum, q_j a=u_j b and u_j is a unit, so b=u_j^(-1)q_j a∈J. Hence Rb⊆J and J=Rb. Finally the decomposition M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i from N003 becomes M_R=⊕_{i∈I}R b e_i. These vectors span, and are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex independent. They therefore form an R-basis. Export only existence of such b, discharging the private choices a,g,q and their identities.

argument.text: Every integer denominator of an element of R is prime to p, so its image in the characteristic-p field K is nonzero by H001. Thus ρ:R→K, ρ(a/b)=ā b̄^(-1), is a well-defined ring map; equality of fractions and the ring laws follow by cross multiplication. Its kernel is pR and its residue field is Z/pZ: ρ(a/b)=0 exactly when p divides a. Define φ: M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse takes (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. Both maps respect all tensor balancing relations and are inverse on pure tensors, which span. Also η:z⊗c↦(z mod pM_R)⊗c identifies M_R⊗_R K with (M_R/pM_R)⊗_(Z/pZ)K. The inverse sends (z mod pM_R)⊗c to z⊗c; changing z by p times a vector gives zero because pK=0, and all remaining balancing relations follow from ρ. These are the two natural isomorphisms of the supplied proof. H005 gives xM,yM⊆M and H003 gives h=xy-yx, hence hM⊆M. Tensoring these lattice operators commutes with φ and η by their formulas. The induced h equals h_K=x_Ky_K-y_Kx_K. The induced brackets therefore give the L_K-action, including characteristic 2.

produces.statement: ρ:R→K has kernel pR and residue field Z/pZ. The displayed maps φ:V_K≅M_R⊗_R K and η:M_R⊗_R K≅(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(Z/pZ)K are K-linear isomorphisms commuting with all induced lattice-preserving operators. In particular x_K,y_K,h_K are the induced actions of x,y,h and give the L_K-action.

argument.text: Choose b from N004 and define B_i=φ^(-1)((b e_i)⊗1). The R-coordinate isomorphism M_R≅R^I given by the basis (b e_i) tensors to K^I; tensoring its coordinate maps gives inverse coefficient maps, proving that B is a K-basis, not merely a spanning family. Alternatively its reduction is a basis of M_R/pM_R over Z/pZ and then extends to K, via F001. N001 gives the matrices of x,y,h on e_i, and complex linearity gives the same matrices on b e_i. Their coefficients are integers, so extension along ρ and transport by φ give exactly x_K B_0=0, x_K B_i=(λ-i+1)B_(i-1) for i≥1, y_K B_i=(i+1)B_(i+1) for i<λ, y_K B_λ=0, and h_K B_i=(λ-2i)B_i, with integer coefficients read in K. Also n>0 by N001.

argument.text: For every r with 0≤r≤λ<p, none of 1,...,r is divisible by p, so r! is nonzero in K by H001. Define A_r=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r and C_r=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r. On M the identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold; all these operators preserve M by H005. After extension they show that the induced X_r,Y_r are exactly A_r,C_r. For i,j∈I, N002 expresses E_ij as a composition of R-lattice operators and the unit binom(λ,j)^(-1). Its extension, transported by φ, sends B_j to B_i and every other B-coordinate to zero, hence is the map T_ij defined from F002. The image of that unit under ρ remains a unit and is the inverse of the coefficient binom(λ,j) in K, so this coefficient is nonzero. Substituting the just established induced divided powers in N002 gives T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) A_(λ-i) C_λ A_λ C_(λ-j). This proves every exported clause of N005 without comparing reduced weights.

argument.text: By N005 choose B and its matrix units T. There are n=λ+1>0 basis vectors, so V_K≠0. Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. Invariance under x_K and y_K implies invariance under their nonnegative powers and scalar multiples, so under every A_r,C_r in N005. Composing these operators and multiplying by binom(λ,j)^(-1) shows, using the N005 identity, that every T_ij preserves W. This assertion holds for all i,j∈I. By classical cases W=0 or W≠0. Under the zero branch L3: W=0, the desired disjunction holds immediately, and L3 is discharged. In the remaining branch assume L2: W≠0; then there exists a nonzero vector of W.

argument.text: Choose 0≠w∈W using F001 and expand w=Σ_{i∈I}c_i B_i in the basis N005. If every c_i were zero then the expansion would give w=0, a contradiction. Thus there exists an index j∈I with c_j≠0.

argument.text: Choose such j by F002. For arbitrary i∈I, the matrix-unit definition gives T_ij w=c_j B_i. By F001 this vector is in W, and c_j is invertible in the field K. Hence B_i=c_j^(-1)T_ij w∈W. All basis vectors belong to W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 and combine with the zero branch to obtain W=0 or W=V_K under L1. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. By N005 the operators are the induced lattice actions, and by H003 the integer span of x,y,h is closed under bracket; the induced action is the stated L_K-action. Its invariant subspaces are exactly the subspaces invariant under these three generators. H005 ensures these are the actions on the original arbitrary lattice tensor product V_K. Finally H001 permits λ=0 (all factorials and binomial coefficients used equal one) and permits p=2 with λ=0 or 1. None of the argument required distinct h_K eigenvalues or algebraic closure of K. This proves P in the full original domain.

original_context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and

original_context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

hypotheses.statement: p is a prime integer, K is a field of characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight λ and of complex dimension λ+1.
The Chevalley generators satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h, both in sl2(C) and in the action on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊆V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. No equality with the minimal lattice is assumed.

original_context.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if x_K(W)⊆W, y_K(W)⊆W and h_K(W)⊆W, then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L_K-module, for every field K of characteristic p and every integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

If θ sends it to zero then c/s=0 in C, so c=0, and the tensor is zero. This also gives the usual identification of this tensor product with the localization of J. argument.text: Set r=dim_Q T. Tensor the R-coordinate isomorphism in N003 with Q. The result is a Q-linear isomorphism Q⊗_R M_R≅T^I: tensor the coordinate maps in each direction, and identify Q⊗_R J^I with T^I by q⊗(c_i)_i↦(q⊗c_i)_i, whose inverse sums the tensors supported at one coordinate. Finite I makes these mutually inverse. An R-basis of M_R of n members, supplied by N003, extends to a Q-basis of Q⊗_R M_R; its coefficient maps extend and prove both spanning and independence. Its dimension is therefore n. Apply M001 to the finite product T^I over Q: F001 gives finite dimension, hence a finite basis and finite generation; Q has the strong rank condition by the usual finite independent-family bound. M001 gives dim_Q T^I=Σ_{i∈I}dim_Q T=nr, using |I|=n. Thus n=nr, so r=1 because n>0 by N003. By F001, θ identifies T with a one-dimensional rational subspace of C containing J. In particular, for any nonzero a∈J and any c∈J there is a unique q∈Q with c=qa.

argument.text: Choose 0≠a∈J and a nonempty finite generating family g of nonzero elements of J using N003. By F002, write its members as g_j=q_j a with q_j∈Q×. For each such rational q_j, removing all powers of the prime p from its nonzero integer numerator and denominator gives q_j=p^{d_j}u_j, where d_j∈Z and both u_j and u_j^(-1) lie in R: neither the remaining numerator nor denominator is divisible by p. This is just finite factorization by repeated division of nonzero integers by p, and works for positive or negative exponents and signs. The resulting finite family of integer exponents is nonempty.

produces.statement: g is a nonempty finite R-generating family of J, g_j=q_j a with a≠0 and every q_j∈Q×. Each q_j has a p-order d_j∈Z with q_j=p^{d_j}u_j for a unit u_j∈R. The finite set of these p-orders is nonempty.

argument.text: Let d be the family of exponents from F003 and set u_j=p^(-d_j)q_j, a unit of R for each index j. Let ν=min_j d_j and define b=p^ν a. Since p is prime and a≠0, b≠0. For every generator q_j a, its ratio to b is p^{d_j-ν}u_j∈R because d_j≥ν. Thus J⊆Rb. For an index attaining the minimum, q_j a=u_j b and u_j is a unit, so b=u_j^(-1)q_j a∈J. Hence Rb⊆J and J=Rb. They therefore form an R-basis. Export only existence of such b, discharging the private choices a,g,q and their identities.

\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight

of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
